title: Winback Surge Tactical Playbook
body:
Purpose:
This is a compact, tactical playbook for short-cycle winback and escalation during the 8–12 week window before renewal. Designed as a ‘surge lab’ kit: mix of repeatable checklists, a quick-risk scoring rubric, and two exec-ready artifacts (one-pager briefing + email swipes) to accelerate approvals and action.

Scope and principles:
- Scope: Enterprise & mid-market accounts flagged high-risk by Renewal Health Index or via sales/CS signals. Not intended for long-term CSM strategy docs.
- Principles: speed > perfection for first 30 days, clear ownership, measurable hypotheses for each intervention, and an explicit stop/roll-forward decision at two checkpoints.

Quick definitions (for this playbook):
- Winback Surge: a concentrated set of coordinated interventions over 1–4 weeks to de-risk a renewal.
- Red-team Experiment: run a rapid internal trial of 1–2 interventions with measurable metrics before broader rollout.

Signal triggers (any single OR combinations):
1) Usage decline > 40% month-over-month for key features (product owner flagged)
2) Support volume spike or recurring P1s in last 60 days
3) Executive access requests delayed / postponed QBRs
4) Contract value concentration (top feature mismatch) + CSAT < 6
5) New competitor proof-of-concept announced by customer

Risk scoring rubric (0–100, for rapid triage):
- Usage signal: 0/10/20 (stable/declining/drop to near-zero)
- Support incidents: 0/10/25
- Financial sensitivity (discounts, price increases): 0/10/20
- Exec engagement: 0/15/20 (active/on-agenda/dropped)
- Product fit risk (feature gap): 0/10/15
Weighting is intentionally skewed to incidents, exec contact, and financial sensitivity. Triage bands: 0–24 low, 25–49 medium, 50+ high. If score >=50, launch surge.

Immediate surge checklist (Day 0–3):
- [ ] Rapid assemble: Lead (CSM), Account Exec, Solutions Eng, Support SME, Customer Success Manager II (if applicable).
- [ ] One-page brief populated (use template below) and shared with stakeholders + exec sponsor.
- [ ] Targeted convo: schedule Exec touchpoint within 72 hours (email template in artifacts).
- [ ] Establish measurement baseline: usage, NPS, open P1s, revenue risk estimate.

Tactical play options (pick 2–3, run in parallel):
- Technical Quick Win: deploy config/patch that removes the immediate blocker; owner: Solutions Eng; target: 7 days to deploy and validate.
- Executive Recommit: 30-minute exec call with clear ask (renewal plan + timeline); owner: Account Exec; deliverable: signed commitment memo.
- Feature Swap / Comp Plan: temporary access to alternate feature/plan to cover gap for renewal period; owner: Product-led CS; deliverable: short-term credit or promo.
- Usage Re-activation Campaign: targeted in-app guides + success outreach to top 50 users; owner: CSM Ops; metric: MAU change in 14 days.
- SLA/Support Acceleration Contract: offer elevated support for next 6 weeks to stabilize incidents; owner: Support Manager; metric: open ticket closure rate.

Red-team experiment framework (2-week run):
- Hypothesis: e.g., "Scheduling a 20-min executive alignment call increases renewal intent by 20% in 30 days."
- Treatment cohort: 10 accounts (matched by ARR and usage)
- Control cohort: 10 comparable accounts
- Success metric: signed intent or 1.5x improvement in NPS increment.
- Stop criteria: no directional improvement after 14 days.

Escalation path and templates:
- Day 3 escalation (to CS Leader): if no exec call scheduled or baseline shows continued decline; include 1-page brief + top 3 asks.
- Day 7 escalation (VP level): if customer declines calls or incidents persist without remedy; require Exec summary + recommended commercial concessions (if any).
- When to route to Legal/Finance: any contract renegotiation requests beyond standard terms, or if customer signals procurement/legal friction.

Executive one-pager template (fill these fields):
- Account: [name], ARR: [$], Renewal date: [YYYY-MM-DD]
- Current risk score: [#]
- Key signals: bullets (usage, incidents, exec drop-off)
- Urgent asks: (1) Who we want on call, (2) Proposed fix, (3) Commercial ask
- Proposed timeline & decision points: Day 0/7/14
- Measurable outcomes: (usage delta, tickets closed, verbal/LOI)

Suggested executive email subject and body (swipe):
Subject: Quick alignment on [Customer] renewal + stabilization plan
Body: Hi [Exec Name],
We’re seeing specific risk signals on the [Customer] renewal (renewal [date]). I’ve attached a 1-pager with the current state and our recommended 14-day stabilization plan. Request: 20 minutes this week to confirm alignment and surface any items you want prioritized. Proposed times: [2 options].

Owner assignments & RACI (minimum):
- Lead CSM: single thread owner, responsible for customer comms and runbook execution.
- Account Exec: commercial permissions and escalation access.
- Solutions Eng: technical fixes and timelines.
- Support SME: ticket prioritization and SLA changes.
- CS Ops: tracking experiments and metrics reporting.

Measurement cadence and decision gates:
- Daily: ticket status / critical incidents (internal ops lead)
- 72 hours: checkpoint—are we seeing directional improvement? If no, escalate to CS Leader.
- 14 days: decision gate—continue surge (extend another 7–14 days with new hypothesis) OR transition to longer remediation plan OR accept likely churn and prepare close-out activities.

Commercial concession guidance (playbook constraints):
- Small allowances (credits <= 5% ARR) can be approved by AE + CS Leader.
- Discounts or term changes > 5% ARR must be escalated to VP Sales + Finance and documented in Confluence/Jira.
- Any permanent SKU changes require Product sign-off.

Experiment log table (quick format to paste into tracker):
- Experiment Name | Start | Owner | Hypothesis | Metric | Outcome (pass/fail/ongoing)
- ex: Exec-Align-Call | 2024-11-11 | AE:Marco | 20-min call -> 20% uplift intent | LOI rate | ongoing

Common pitfalls & anti-patterns:
- Too many simultaneous concessions without measurement.
- Pulling in legal/commercial too late (use early if procurement engaged).
- Leaving ownership ambiguous at handoffs (always set a single CSM owner).

Templates and artifacts to attach to surge initiation:
- One-pager brief (required)
- Exec email swipe (required)
- Ticket snapshot export (support)
- Usage trend chart (last 90 days)
- Short-term commercial approval form (CS Leader sign-off)

Next steps to use this doc (for CSMs running a surge):
1) Duplicate this doc and populate one-pager.
2) Run quick risk score and choose up to 3 interventions.
3) Book Exec call and post brief in #cs-urgent-saves Slack.
4) Log experiments in tracker and reassess at Day 3/14 gates.

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- Want feedback on whether the 14-day cadence is too aggressive for large enterprises—I’m leaning fast because we need signal before procurement cycles.
- Recommend CS Ops provide a canned GA report for the Usage trend chart to avoid manual exports.
- Marco suggested an optional ‘relationship reset’ dinner for strategic accounts; keep as tertiary play.

Appendix: sample filled one-pager (example):
Account: Graystone Financial | ARR: $420k | Renewal: 2025-02-28 | Risk score: 62
Key signals: sustained 55% decline in reconciliation job runs; 3 P1s in last 30 days; VP product missed QBR 2x
Immediate asks: Exec call w/VP product + PM, temporary credit for downtime (3%), priority SLA for 30 days.
Plan: Tech fix for job failures (3 days), Exec alignment call (within 72h), Usage reactivation campaign (14 days).
Success metrics: job run rate +40% within 7 days, 0 P1s in 14 days, verbal intent to renew by Day 14.

End of document.
